decision.explanation: Using ln((1+x)/(1-4x)) = ln(1+x) - ln(1-4x), the expansion is (x-x²/2+x³/3)+(4x+8x²+64x³/3)=5x+15x²/2+65x³/3+⋯. Thus option e gives the first three non-zero terms.

after.name: Question 1
after.problem: Find the first three non-zero terms of the Maclaurin expansion of $\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{1+x}{1-4x}).$
after.worked_solution:
First, using the laws of logarithms, we observe that

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{1+x}{1-4x}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(1+x)-\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-4x).\end{aligned}
$$

For the expansion of $\operatorname{ln}⁡(1+x),$ we recall the standard result

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡(1+x) & =x-\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}+\frac{{x}^{3}}{3}-⋯.\end{aligned}
$$

To obtain the expansion of $\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-4x),$ we replace $x$ with $-4x$ in the standard expansion:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-4x) & =(-4x)-\frac{(-4x)^{2}}{2}+\frac{(-4x)^{3}}{3}-⋯ \\  & =-4x-8{x}^{2}-\frac{64{x}^{3}}{3}-⋯.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, subtracting the expansion for $\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-4x)$ from the expansion for $\operatorname{ln}⁡(1+x),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{1+x}{1-4x}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(1+x)-\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-4x) \\  & =(x-\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}+\frac{{x}^{3}}{3}-⋯)-(-4x-8{x}^{2}-\frac{64{x}^{3}}{3}-⋯) \\  & =(1+4)x+(-\frac{1}{2}+8){x}^{2}+(\frac{1}{3}+\frac{64}{3}){x}^{3}+⋯ \\  & =5x+\frac{15{x}^{2}}{2}+\frac{65{x}^{3}}{3}+⋯\end{aligned}
$$

content.problem: Find the first three non-zero terms of the Maclaurin expansion of $\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{1+x}{1-4x}).$
content.worked_solution:
First, using the laws of logarithms, we observe that

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{1+x}{1-4x}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(1+x)-\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-4x).\end{aligned}
$$

For the expansion of $\operatorname{ln}⁡(1+x),$ we recall the standard result

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡(1+x) & =x-\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}+\frac{{x}^{3}}{3}-⋯.\end{aligned}
$$

To obtain the expansion of $\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-4x),$ we replace $x$ with $-4x$ in the standard expansion:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-4x) & =(-4x)-\frac{(-4x)^{2}}{2}+\frac{(-4x)^{3}}{3}-⋯ \\  & =-4x-8{x}^{2}-\frac{64{x}^{3}}{3}-⋯.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, subtracting the expansion for $\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-4x)$ from the expansion for $\operatorname{ln}⁡(1+x),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{1+x}{1-4x}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(1+x)-\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-4x) \\  & =(x-\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}+\frac{{x}^{3}}{3}-⋯)-(-4x-8{x}^{2}-\frac{64{x}^{3}}{3}-⋯) \\  & =(1+4)x+(-\frac{1}{2}+8){x}^{2}+(\frac{1}{3}+\frac{64}{3}){x}^{3}+⋯ \\  & =5x+\frac{15{x}^{2}}{2}+\frac{65{x}^{3}}{3}+⋯\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡(1+x)=x-\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}+\frac{1}{3}{x}^{3}-⋯.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-\frac{3x}{4}) & =(-\frac{3x}{4})-\frac{1}{2}{(-\frac{3x}{4})}^{2}+\frac{1}{3}{(-\frac{3x}{4})}^{3}-⋯ \\  & =-\frac{3x}{4}-\frac{1}{2}(\frac{9{x}^{2}}{16})+\frac{1}{3}(-\frac{27{x}^{3}}{64})-⋯ \\  & =-\frac{3x}{4}-\frac{9{x}^{2}}{32}-\frac{9{x}^{3}}{64}-⋯.\end{aligned}

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡(4-3x) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(4)+\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-\frac{3x}{4}) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(4)+(-\frac{3x}{4}-\frac{9{x}^{2}}{32}-\frac{9{x}^{3}}{64}-⋯) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(4)-\frac{3x}{4}-\frac{9{x}^{2}}{32}-\frac{9{x}^{3}}{64}-⋯\end{aligned}
